summary: Port reproduces the pattern's architecture and rhythm (a centred N-petal flower with a contrasting-hue core, redrawn every ~2.5-2.7 s after a ~1 s animated phase and a ~1.5 s freeze) but draws it at roughly half the radius as thin hollow petal outlines, and its flower never rotates while the original's spins steadily.
observations: Both sides are alive, error-free and steady out to at least t=192 s (label `late`, --skip 180): orig meanBrightness avg 16, port avg 5, both still cycling normally; neither dies or saturates.

Shared temporal architecture: each cycle is ~1 s of animation followed by a genuine freeze (motion exactly 0 for the whole hold). Orig at 20 fps: active frames 1-20, frozen 21-50, repeating with period exactly 50 frames. Port: active 33-53, frozen 54-86, period 54 frames. Duty cycle matches (orig 40% active, port 39%).

Cycle period: orig is exactly 2.50 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps (25/50/100 frames) — fully fps-invariant. Port is 2.80 s / 2.70 s / 2.65 s at 10/20/40 fps, i.e. ~2.6 s plus a 2-frame overshoot per cycle. So the port's cycle runs 6-12% long and is mildly frame-rate coupled where the original is not.

SIZE (biggest structural gap). On a 48x48 grid (inscribed radius 24) the original's petals reach outer radius 19-25 — they fill and often overflow the frame; the port's reach 7-15 (median ~10.7), i.e. ~45-55% of the original's radius. Lit-pixel fraction at matched times: orig 43.4%/37.6%/63.8%, port 8.5%/3.1%/4.0%. On the default 16x16 rig the same gap shows as orig lighting 35-102 of 256 px versus port 8-22.

This is a size difference, not a brightness bug: per-lit-pixel brightness is comparable (orig ~63 vs port ~68 mean-of-max over lit pixels at t=0.7 s) and both sides hit near-full peaks (orig max 255, port max 243). The 4x gap in whole-rig meanBrightness (orig 12-20, port 3-6) is almost entirely explained by the smaller lit area.

PETAL FORM. Original petals are solid, smoothly shaded lobes that meet each other near the core; the port's are thin outlined slivers with a dark interior and a visible gap between the petal bases and the centre dot. On the 16x16 default rig this makes the port read as a handful of scattered isolated pixels while the original reads as a filled flower.

CENTRE. Radial profiles at 48x48 (mean value per integer radius): orig r1=7/16/11, r2=32/80/57, r3=43/119/85, r4=24/89/63, r5=55/29/21 — a broad bright annulus with a DARK core and a gap before the petals. Port: r1=131/117/87, r2=56/49/37, r3=32/5/6 — a small solid bright dot, no dark core. Both then show the petal ring, so the core-gap-petals architecture is right but the core is drawn differently.

ROTATION (biggest motion gap). During the animated phase the original's flower advances by a constant angle every rendered frame: 360-bin angular cross-correlation gives 58.75 deg/frame at 20, 40, 100 and 500 fps, and in another cycle a steady -90.0 deg/frame for 17 consecutive frames with relative frame-to-frame profile change pinned at 0.56-0.61. It is frame-stepped, so the apparent spin rate scales with frame rate (~3.3 rev/s at the default 20 fps).

The port's flower does not rotate at all: net angular shift 0.00 deg (0.25 deg resolution) across 0.02 s of 0.002 s steps at 500 fps, and no consistent sign across a whole active phase at 20 fps. Its animation is an in-place shimmer of the thin petal outlines — per-frame relative profile change 0.74-1.06 (higher than the original's 0.56-0.61) but with no net direction. motionLit avg 29.5 (port) vs 12.3 (orig) in the late window reflects the same thing: the port churns its few lit pixels harder while going nowhere.

Colour family matches. Both draw petals and core in near-complementary hues (orig e.g. core 252deg / petals 93deg, 25/168, 241/12; port 198/346, 329/160, 352/187) and both walk through a fresh hue pair every cycle across blues, greens, teals, magentas, golds and reds. No palette-family divergence found over 60 s and three seeds.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way: re-rendered at 8x8, 16x16 and 48x48 each draws the same logical flower, coarser or finer, with no change in feature count. The size ratio between them is preserved at all three grid sizes (at 8x8 the original fills the panel edge to edge while the port occupies a ~3x3 central patch).

Start-up: at t=0 the original is fully black and blooms into a bright first cycle (meanBrightness 0 -> 28 within one frame at 20 fps); the port is already drawn at t=0 and starts inside a frozen hold, its first animated phase beginning ~1.6 s in. Minor, and partly a phase offset rather than a behaviour difference.

Seeds 1, 7 and 1234 all show the same picture on both sides (orig full-frame filled petals with a broad dark-cored disc; port half-size thin outlined petals with a solid dot), so none of the above is a one-seed fluke.
Control surface: the harness reports NO settable controls on either side, and --probe-controls confirms it ('no settable controls' for both). No control-surface mismatch.
feedback: Scale the flower up by ~2x. Measured on a 48x48 grid the original's petals reach outer radius 19-25 of a 24-px inscribed radius (they fill or overflow the panel); the port's reach only 7-15. Same ratio holds at 8x8 and 16x16, so it is a fixed scale factor on the logical flower, not a rasterisation effect. Target: the petal tips should touch the panel edge in most cycles.

Fill the petals. The original's petals are solid lobes with a smooth brightness gradient that fade toward the tips and meet each other near the core; the port draws only thin outlines with dark interiors. At matched times the original lights 38-64% of the grid, the port 3-9%. Per-pixel brightness already matches (~63 vs ~68 over lit pixels), so this is about area/fill, not gain — do not simply brighten.

Add the missing spin. The original's flower advances a CONSTANT angle every rendered frame during its ~1 s animated phase — 58.75 deg/frame measured identically at 20, 40, 100 and 500 fps, i.e. frame-stepped, ~3.3 rev/s at the default 20 fps. The port's flower holds a fixed orientation (net 0.00 deg over 0.02 s at 500 fps) and only shimmers its petal outlines in place. This is the pattern's defining motion and it is currently absent.

Fix the core. The original's centre is a broad disc (bright annulus peaking around radius 3 of 24, values 43-119) with a DARK hole in the middle, then a dark gap, then the petals. The port's centre is a small solid bright dot peaking at radius 1 (values 87-131) with no dark core. Widen it and punch out the middle.

Trim the cycle to exactly 2.50 s and make it frame-rate independent. Original: 1.00 s animated + 1.50 s frozen, identical at 10/20/40 fps. Port: ~1.0 s + ~1.6 s plus a 2-frame overshoot, giving 2.80/2.70/2.65 s at 10/20/40 fps. The hold is ~7% too long and the cycle boundary is counted in frames rather than time.
Minor: the original opens on black and blooms in its first cycle; the port is already drawn at t=0 and starts mid-hold. Worth matching once the above are fixed, but it is the smallest of the gaps.
